sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. 2017. Hezhang Buyi: a highly endangered Northern Tai language with a Kra substratum. Manuscript (revised from a paper presented at ICSTLL 46, Dartmouth, 2013), 26 pp. Zenodo. doi:10.5281/zenodo.1249176
sources.note: Nothing on Maza prosody. The Maza material is two glossed clauses with Chao tone digits (ŋa²¹ ma²¹za³⁵ la⁵³ 'I am Maza'; ŋa²¹ ma²¹za³⁵ ma²¹ ŋuɛ³⁵ xa³³ 'I am not Maza', circumfixal negation ma²¹.. xa³³) plus remarks on the Kra (Qabiao) substratum and location; the paper's 'Tones' section (2.3) is about Hezhang Buyi's five tones. No Maza tone inventory, no mention of stress or accent for Maza; readers are referred to Hsiu (2014), already read and silent.

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. 2017. Maza audio word list (c. 190 wav files, single words and short phrases, recorded 22 April 2013). Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.1123369
sources.note: The only primary data on Maza; disyllables (e.g. compound nouns, 'i-am-maza', numeral phrases) could be inspected acoustically for prominence, but it contains no descriptive statement — would only support a first-hand instrumental judgement, not a quotable rule.

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. 2014. Mondzish: a new subgroup of Lolo-Burmese. In Proceedings of the 14th International Symposium on Chinese Languages and Linguistics (IsCLL-14), 62-81. Taipei: Institute of Linguistics, Academia Sinica. doi:10.5281/zenodo.1127814
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2.4-2.4.1 'Maza' (pp. 8-10) gives location, <50 speakers, Kra/Qabiao loan stratum; only phonological remark: 'Maza does not allow for final stops and vowel length like most other Lolo-Burmese languages'. Tones as Chao digits on all forms; no stress/accent statement anywhere in the paper.
